column1: # tests/tapebin-expected.tsv -- the archived Python tape codec's verdicts on every tape probe, frozen 2026-10-23 at
# e3c4b123 while the seed was still importable (plans/unisa-detach.md W1-G, rule R1).  It replaces the per-run calls of
# the seed codec's encode in the com-tapebin-K shards (tests/tapebinproduct.cx TAPEBIN_SHARD=K/6) and in
# One row per probe (examples/*.c then tests/c/*.c, sorted, as the shards list them) and target: the two gate hosts
# lnx/x86_64 and osx/arm64, and all six targets for examples/hello.c.  For TEXT = the classic reference's tape
# (`UA PROBE -t TARGET`, UA built by tests/build_ref.sh from the same tree):
#   origin  sha256(encode(TEXT, origin_target=target_id(TARGET)))   -- also what `UA PROBE -t TARGET --tapebin` wrote
#   zero    sha256(encode(TEXT))                                     -- the carrier of the same text with no origin
# each the first 32 hex digits.  There is no regeneration path (the codec is archived).  When a compiler change moves
# a probe's tape, its row no longer judges anything and the shard says so (red, with the row the C codecs would give);
# re-pinning that row from the C reference is a deliberate, reviewed act and the row then stops being an independent
